detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: BACnet gateway (e.g. Cimetrics BACstac, Contemporary Controls), Splunk Edge Hub, custom scripted input.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=bms:bacnet`, `sourcetype=bms:hvac`.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest AHU BACnet points via Edge Hub or BACnet gateway. Compare supply air temperature to setpoint. Alert on sustained deviation >2°F/1°C.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=building sourcetype="bms:hvac" object_type="AHU"
| eval delta=abs(supply_air_temp - supply_air_setpoint)
| bin _time span=15m
| stats avg(delta) as avg_deviation, max(delta) as max_deviation, avg(supply_air_temp) as avg_supply, latest(supply_air_setpoint) as setpoint by ahu_name, _time
| where avg_deviation > 2
| table _time, ahu_name, setpoint, avg_supply, avg_deviation, max_deviation
```

Understanding this SPL

**AHU Supply Air Temperature Deviation** — Air Handling Unit supply air temperature drifting from setpoint indicates coil fouling, valve failures, or economizer faults — wasting energy and degrading occupant comfort. Catching deviations early prevents complaints and energy waste.

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=bms:bacnet`, `sourcetype=bms:hvac`. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): BACnet gateway (e.g. Cimetrics BACstac, Contemporary Controls), Splunk Edge Hub, custom scripted input. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: building; **sourcetype**: bms:hvac. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=building, sourcetype="bms:hvac". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **delta** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Discretizes time or numeric ranges with `bin`/`bucket`.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by ahu_name, _time** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• Filters the current rows with `where avg_deviation > 2` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.
• Pipeline stage (see **AHU Supply Air Temperature Deviation**): table _time, ahu_name, setpoint, avg_supply, avg_deviation, max_deviation


Step 3 — Validate
Run the search in a known window. Spot-check a few events against the BMS console (for example Niagara, Tridium, or Honeywell) and confirm zones, values, and alarms line up. Verify field names and that the right roles can search the index.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Line chart (supply temp vs setpoint per AHU); deviation heatmap by AHU and time of day; single value (worst deviation).
